body:
Closing as not reproducible.

## What was tested

The duplicate-key error does not fire even once during app-shell boot — on current `main` (`9b773f976`) **or** on `b0760501a` (#2930), the commit this was filed against.

| Axis | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Commit | `9b773f976` (main) / `b0760501a` (#2930) |
| Backend | own `--fresh` app-showcase, and a long-lived persistent app-showcase DB |
| Console wiring | `VITE_SERVER_URL=` + dev proxy, and the default `.env.development` direct-to-:3000 (the setup in the report) |
| Locale | `en-US` / `zh-CN` |
| Viewport | desktop 1440 / mobile 390 |
| Routes | `/system/approvals`, `/home`, `/apps/{showcase_app,setup,account,crm_enterprise}`, `/studio`, `/ai`, object lists, `metadata`, `/organizations`, `/docs`, system + developer pages — hard loads and SPA back/forward |
| Interactions | ⌘K command palette, `?` shortcuts dialog, sidebar collapse / mobile drawer |

The detector itself is known-good: planting one pair of same-key siblings in `ConsoleLayout` produced **6** of these errors on a single boot, captured by the same listener that reports zero for the unmodified tree.

Also ruled out along the way:

- No duplicate `id` in any app's navigation tree (58 / 51 / 10 / 19 items across the four apps).
- No duplicate `name` or `id` across `object` / `view` / `app` / `dashboard` / `page` / `report` metadata.
- All ten locale packs have three distinct `console.loadingSteps` strings (`LoadingScreen` keys by the translated string).
- `b0760501a..HEAD` touches exactly **one** `key=` line in app-shell / layout / components / console (an addition in `select.tsx`) — so this was not incidentally fixed in between.

## Correction to the suggested next step

Capturing "the owner component name in the error's trailing argument" will not work: React 19 logs this error with **no component stack**, only two arguments —

```
Encountered two children with the same key, `%s`. …
dupkey-probe
```

The actionable signal is the **second argument — the duplicated key value** (`dupkey-probe` above), which points straight at the offending `.map`.

## If it comes back

Temporarily prepend this to `apps/console/src/main.tsx` and reload:

```ts
const _e = console.error;
console.error = (...a: any[]) => {
  if (typeof a[0] === 'string' && a[0].includes('same key')) _e('[dupkey]', a[1]);
  _e(...a);
};
```

Reopen with the printed key value and it can be fixed directly.
